purpose: Follow two newly located original handoff trails from a specific sender artifact through content-specific recipient use, then test participant identity, operator separation, authorization, prior reporting and alternative explanations before promotion.

safety.publication_note: Only public GitHub records, immutable Git identifiers, content hashes, event and observation times, domain-level summaries and limitations are retained. Personal addresses, secrets, tokens, raw prompts, private logs and executable payload bodies are omitted.

paused_backlog_state.reason_not_reopened: The unread remainder remains fully classified as comparison overlap, known-family control, or the known Amap and DseWiki host controls. Neither selected public Git trail supplies a source-level cue separating one paused scanner record into a new episode.

locator_scope.counting_note: The 142 returned rows are locator occurrences, not 142 episodes. The capped query is not exhaustive. The two selected trails were chosen because their immutable records expose a named source, transferred task material and later content-specific use; other visible rows were designed teams, review workflows, implementation records or documentation controls.

selected_original_records.title: DRTS tenant-governance contract to tenant-commute-hub implementation

source_record.message_role: Finalizes the tenant-governance API documentation used as the receiving repository's locked contract. The message labels LLM-Agent Codex2 and Reviewer Claude2; those project-authored labels conflict with the Git author label and are not identity attestations.

source_authorization_artifacts.role: Primary machine-truth snapshot. It registers TCH-SDK-BUMP-001 as a cross-repository placeholder, assigns both owner and reviewer to cross-repo, names the three recipient UI surfaces, states the backend dependencies and says the actual work belongs in tenant-commute-hub.
Public acceptance packet that allocates the cost-center, approval-rule, quota and approval-request surfaces to the receiving repository and forbids inventing local contract semantics.
Pre-existing planning record for the cross-repository UI integration.

transfer_record.role: Explicit handoff-received checkpoint. It locks the source commit, replaces the recipient's iteration-zero spec with three concrete iteration-one scopes and regenerates the shared contract snapshot.

transfer_artifacts.role: Pins the exact source repository and commit and records TCH-SDK-BUMP-001.
Machine-readable recipient task containing the three exact UI scopes and the source contract version.

Governance record describing the intended GitHub-driven closed loop: source LLM writes a spec, automation copies it to the recipient, the recipient implements it, feedback is dispatched back and the source orchestrator continues.

recipient_use_records.role: Direct child implements the transferred cost-center methods, page and coverage report.
Implements the transferred approval-rule CRUD, reorder and dry-run scope.
Implements the transferred booking cost-center selection, quota preview and named error handling.
Closes the iteration, maps each transferred scope to its implementation commit and expressly hands feedback back to the source supervisor.
Content-specific closeout names all three implementation commits, reports the exact completed scopes and asks the source supervisor to choose the next iteration.

candidate_source_record.role: Later source-side squash merge initially located by the TCH task marker.

basis: The ai-status.json in 75ce143 is byte-identical to the source-contract snapshot: both use Git blob 874e36cfc4773aff89266bb0e077825f735d8568.
That snapshot says updated_at 2026-05-13T12:23:02Z and leaves TCH-SDK-BUMP-001 blocked with a 13 May last update, before the 14 May transfer and closeout.
Neither TCH-SDK-CONSUME-001 nor recipient closeout 43fbf4e appears in the later snapshot, any searched source revision or the current default branch.

At current source head ca6c6937998b83a5cbcc2c0d6a22472657932ba2, .ai-loop-incoming contains only .gitkeep. The public receiver workflow defines the intended dispatch-to-commit return path, but no resulting feedback file is present.
return_path_check.missing_evidence: A public source commit that imports the 43fbf4e feedback artifact or marks TCH-SDK-CONSUME-001 complete. The outbound transfer and recipient implementation are verified; source-side consumption is not.

dependency_assessment.temporal: The transfer commit follows the source contract by 10 hours 18 minutes 31 seconds. Its direct child begins implementation 5 minutes 7 seconds later, and the three slices plus closeout form one uninterrupted five-commit chain.
dependency_assessment.semantic: High confidence. The recipient pins the exact source SHA, imports the named contract surface, implements all three assigned scopes and returns a commit-anchored feedback artifact.
dependency_assessment.verified_participants: Two inconsistent Git author/model-label sets are visible, but neither is a provider-owned run attestation. The receiver's Git identity says Gemini2 while its messages self-label Claude; the source commit's Git identity says Claude while its message labels Codex2 and Claude2 roles.
dependency_assessment.operator_boundary: Not established. Both repositories are in the same public GitHub namespace, the source task explicitly assigns the work to the receiving repository, and the receiving repository documents the exchange as an intended automated closed loop.
dependency_assessment.current_activity: Historical May sequence; no claim that any named runtime remains active.

alternative_tests.basis: The machine-truth placeholder, acceptance packet, recipient spec and .ai-loop README predefine the transfer, roles, files, return path and task scope.

alternative_tests.alternative: single operator using several local agent labels
alternative_tests.result: not excluded and favored over independent operators
alternative_tests.basis: Both repositories share one owner namespace, every receiving commit uses one Git author label, and project-authored model labels conflict with Git labels.
Every implementation commit maps to one of the three transferred scopes; the closeout records deferrals instead of acting beyond the iteration.

selected_original_records.title: WB004 correction handoff to the BNROSE Rust execution lane

source_record.role: Records a retry-safety correction at source, transfers chain receipts and a deterministic reference regression to the Rust lane, and archives the sending lane.

source_pull_request.role: Primary public task record. It states a founder ruling, defines the correction and persistence law, assigns the handoff to the BNROSE-RUST-001/SETTLE owner, forbids a new JavaScript signer and says the lane archives after merge.

handoff_artifact.role: Merged handoff version after source commit dcdf503 and same-branch rider c1d0766. It names the sending seat, founder ruling, exact evidence package, required persistence behavior, prohibited replacement behavior, compatibility vectors, preserved findings and the receiving Rust lane.

recipient_use_record.role: Explicit handoff-received record. It says the receiving lane read the named handoff and regression in full, verifies three source-inspection findings, implements ordered steps under one authorization, adds recovery and adversarial rows, and routes a separate timeout issue onward.

recipient_artifact.role: Maps the transferred retry-safety rules to concrete Rust implementation and test changes and expressly records the receiving owner.

recipient_lane_authorization.role: Public receiving-lane task says the build follows the founder order, records ownership before the run, bounds claims to a single supervisor, reports no human interaction during execution and names an authorized merger as next owner.

same_custodian_reuse_check.result: content-specific later reuse, but no new operator-boundary transfer
same_custodian_reuse_check.basis: The later SOVEXEC-002 lane reuses the WB004 custody kit and explicitly follows the 13 October correction's one-push-per-step and no-replacement-on-uncertain-outcome law. Its record says the founder ordered the lane in the current session; the same public account and repository publish it. This advances the content-use cursor but does not identify a separately controlled recipient.

dependency_assessment.temporal: The recipient authored its handoff-use record 22 minutes 55 seconds after the source PR merged; its branch was later rebased and committed after the receiving PR merge, so author and committer times are retained separately.
dependency_assessment.semantic: High confidence. The recipient names the exact handoff, reads its source findings, adopts its persistence/refusal rules and implements matching Rust paths and tests.
dependency_assessment.verified_participants: One public GitHub account authors both source and recipient commits. Lane and agent numbers are project roles, not independently authenticated principals.
dependency_assessment.operator_boundary: Not crossed. A founder ruling assigns the transfer, both PRs pre-record lane ownership, and one public account carries both sides inside one repository.
dependency_assessment.current_activity: Historical 13 October sequence; no claim that a runtime or lane remains active.

alternative_tests.basis: Both PR bodies and both dispatch files identify the founder ruling, receiving lane, allowed evidence and prohibited actions before recipient use.

alternative_tests.alternative: same human or same operator publishing several role voices
alternative_tests.result: not excluded and strongly supported by provenance
alternative_tests.basis: The same public GitHub account authors the source correction, handoff and recipient-use commit.

alternative_tests.alternative: the phrase 'a genuinely new supervisor' proves a second real participant
alternative_tests.basis: In context it describes a recovery test scenario reconstructed from a journal, not a public message sender, account, provider run or separate operator.
The recipient implements the exact persistence and retry-safety duties transferred by PR 408, leaves separately owned work untouched and routes the timeout issue to its assigned lane.

cross_record_assessment.reason: The original records establish exactly the transfer-and-use dependency the investigation seeks, but also preserve the contrary evidence needed to reject promotion: preassigned tasks, explicit owner/founder authorization, same-namespace or same-account custody and recipient actions bounded to the transferred scope.

evidence_needed_to_advance: Provider- or operator-owned attestations binding exact sender and recipient runs to independently controlled principals.
Primary evidence that a recipient acted outside the published closed-loop task, founder ruling, assigned lane, branch, issue, review or merge authority.

Separate primary evidence of subjective rogue intent; none is currently present.
